title: 4.4 The Menstrual Cycle
description: Phases of the menstrual cycle, hormones involved, and the 28-day cycle

questions.question: The menstrual cycle refers to approximately monthly changes in the:
questions.explanation: The approximately monthly changes in the uterus are referred to as the menstrual cycle.

questions.question: The first day of the menstrual cycle is marked by the onset of:
questions.explanation: The first day of the menstrual cycle is marked by the onset of menstruation, which is the flow of bits of uterine lining and blood.

questions.question: During menstruation, what is shed from the body?
options: Bits of uterine lining and some blood
questions.correctAnswer: Bits of uterine lining and some blood
questions.explanation: Menstruation is the flow of bits of uterine lining and some blood from the uterus, through the cervix, and out of the vagina.

questions.question: The first phase of the menstrual cycle, during which bleeding occurs, is called the:
questions.explanation: The flow phase is the first phase of the menstrual cycle, marked by menstruation.

questions.question: The interval of follicle maturation before ovulation is the:
questions.explanation: The interval of follicle maturation before ovulation is the follicular phase of the cycle.

questions.question: During the follicular phase, cells around the egg secrete which hormone that stimulates the endometrium to thicken?
questions.explanation: During the follicular phase, cells around the egg secrete estrogens that stimulate the endometrium to thicken.

questions.question: Which hormone triggers ovulation?
questions.explanation: The rise in estrogens encourages the pituitary to release more LH, which causes the follicle to swell and burst — triggering ovulation.

questions.question: The phase that begins after ovulation is the:
questions.explanation: The luteal phase of the cycle begins after ovulation.

questions.question: After ovulation, the ruptured follicle develops into a structure called the:
questions.explanation: After ovulation, cells of the ruptured follicle develop into a hormone-secreting corpus luteum.

questions.question: The corpus luteum secretes which hormones?
questions.explanation: The corpus luteum secretes some estrogens and a lot of progesterone.

questions.question: Progesterone causes the uterine lining to:
options: Thicken and encourage blood vessel growth
questions.correctAnswer: Thicken and encourage blood vessel growth
questions.explanation: Progesterone causes the uterine lining to thicken and encourages blood vessels to grow through it, preparing the uterus for pregnancy.

questions.question: If pregnancy does not occur, what happens to the corpus luteum?
questions.explanation: If pregnancy does not occur, the corpus luteum breaks down, and a new follicle will begin to mature.

questions.question: What happens when the corpus luteum breaks down?
options: A new follicle begins to mature
questions.explanation: When the corpus luteum breaks down, menstruation occurs.

questions.question: The menstrual cycle typically lasts approximately how many days?
questions.explanation: At puberty, hormonal changes prompt eggs to mature one at a time in an approximately twenty-eight-day ovarian cycle.

questions.question: FSH stands for:
questions.explanation: FSH stands for follicle-stimulating hormone, which stimulates the development of follicles in the ovary.

questions.question: FSH stimulates which process in the ovarian cycle?
questions.explanation: FSH stimulates maturation of an ovarian follicle.

questions.question: The hormone that stimulates the release of an egg from the ovary is:
questions.explanation: LH (luteinizing hormone) triggers the release of the egg during ovulation.

questions.question: Estrogen is primarily responsible for:
options: Thickening the uterine lining after ovulation
Development of female secondary sexual characteristics
questions.correctAnswer: Development of female secondary sexual characteristics
questions.explanation: Estrogen triggers development of female secondary sexual characteristics and maintains the lining of the reproductive tract.

questions.question: Menopause occurs when:
options: All follicles in the ovaries have been released or disintegrated
questions.correctAnswer: All follicles in the ovaries have been released or disintegrated
questions.explanation: Menopause occurs when all the follicles in the ovaries have either been released during menstrual cycles or have disintegrated as a result of aging.

questions.question: During menopause, production of estrogen and progesterone is:
questions.explanation: With no follicles left to mature, production of estrogen and progesterone is diminished and menstrual cycles cease.

questions.question: A follicle is best described as:
options: A hormone released by the pituitary
A group of epithelial cells surrounding a developing egg cell
The duct that carries eggs to the uterus
questions.correctAnswer: A group of epithelial cells surrounding a developing egg cell
questions.explanation: A follicle is a group of epithelial cells that surround a developing egg cell.

questions.question: Menstrual hygiene practices include:
options: Wearing tight fabrics to absorb moisture
Using scented products for better hygiene
questions.explanation: Changing menstrual products regularly is important because trapped moisture can provide a breeding ground for bacteria and fungi.

questions.question: The vagina is best described as:
options: An organ that requires regular internal cleaning
A self-cleaning organ that should only be rinsed externally with water
An organ that produces menstrual blood
questions.correctAnswer: A self-cleaning organ that should only be rinsed externally with water
questions.explanation: The vagina is a self-cleaning organ. Only water should be used to rinse the vulva externally.

questions.question: A woman entering menopause is known only in humans and which other species?
questions.explanation: Menopause is known only in humans and two species of whales.
